clue.text: Irritability shown by politician that's given entry to deviant US singer

indicators.note: the politician is let in, so those letters go inside the rearranged ones
deviant means straying from the norm, so the letters of US singer are rearranged

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is the standard abbreviation for a politician

explanation.surface: A crotchety politician lets a wayward American singer into some event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deviant' rearranges US SINGER into GRUINESS, and 'given entry to' puts MP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a bad-tempered, tetchy state of mind, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Pass the fish

definitions.meaning: to ... is to pass, as time or a person passes

explanation.surface: Someone at the table asks for the fish dish to be handed over.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the phrasal verb meaning to pass; the other is the name of a small sea fish.

clue.text: They may come up from boundaries of Uranus

definitions.text: They may come up from boundaries of Uranus

indicators.note: come up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Alien craft might arrive from the far edge of the planet Uranus.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'They may' alone as the definition, which cannot stand for the answer; the whole clue is the definition, since flying saucers may come from beyond Uranus. In a down clue 'come up' reads the hidden letters upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Unidentified flying objects are imagined as alien craft arriving from the outer solar system.

clue.text: Holiday offers for parcels around Kentish Town

indicators.note: the parcels wrap around the town, so its letters go inside

parts.note: parcels are packages
Deal is a seaside town in Kent

explanation.surface: Travel agents' bargains are compared with parcels sent round the London district of Kentish Town.
explanation.walkthrough: Kentish Town is also a district of north London, a false lead: read it as 'a town in Kent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Package holidays bundle travel and lodging at one price, sold as bargain bundles by tour firms.

clue.text: Diana dancing with southern river nymphs

indicators.note: dancing has the letters of Diana moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: The goddess Diana dances with water spirits from the south.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth these are the female spirits of springs, rivers and fountains.

clue.text: Spiders or cricket types?

definitions.meaning: spiders weave webs, so they are makers of thread
in cricket, slow bowlers who make the ball turn are given this name

explanation.surface: A question about whether something is a spider or a cricket, both creepy-crawlies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cricket' looks like the insect beside the spiders; it is the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiders produce silk threads; cricketers who bowl with turn are called by the same word.

clue.text: Asian with some straight hair

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A person from Asia whose hair is partly straight.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Thailand is from South-East Asia, so this is an example of an Asian.

clue.text: He takes his latte out. It does him most good

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase standing for the adjective: what is best for one's well-being

indicators.note: out here means worked out or put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man takes his coffee to go, finding it the most beneficial drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' looks like a takeaway coffee order, but it is the anagram signal for 'his latte'; 'takes' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of the adjective for wholesome or good for the body, so what benefits him most.

clue.text: Heath likely playing Othello

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of likely are performed in a new arrangement

parts.note: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice

explanation.surface: Ted Heath, the Prime Minister, may take the part of Othello on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: ILKLEY Moor is a stretch of moorland in West Yorkshire, famous from the folk song 'On Ilkla Moor Baht 'at'. 'Heath' reads as Edward Heath, the British Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A Yorkshire moor is open upland covered in heather, which is a heath.

clue.text: Eleanor the actress, young girl, is making a complaint

parts.note: Eleanor Bron is an English actress
a chit is a young, often cheeky, girl

explanation.surface: An actress and a young girl are lodging a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: Eleanor Bron is a British actress known from the Beatles film Help! 'complaint' is in the medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint can mean an illness, and this inflammation of the airways in the lungs is one.

clue.text: Stickiness of food

definitions.meaning: the tacky quality of glue or paint that is not quite dry
... is slang for food, as in hard ..., the ship's biscuit

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a dish is gummy.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the adhesive feel of a surface; the other is old sailors' slang for rations.

clue.text: Carol, you, him and me going to college

parts.note: the three people together are we three
King's College, at Cambridge or London

explanation.surface: Three friends go off to university, carol singing on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: King's College, Cambridge, is famous for its Christmas carol service, which fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a well-known Christmas hymn about the Magi, so an example of a carol.

clue.text: Horticulturists' paradise in short road, cryptically

parts.note: RD is short for road, and those two letters are the middle of the word garden

explanation.surface: A place gardeners love, found down a little lane.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer cryptically: the centre of GARDEN is RD, which is 'short road', the wordplay the clue gives.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop selling plants, tools and seeds is a gardener's idea of heaven.

clue.text: Car drivers display costly wraps, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means heard rather than seen, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: to display is to show, and costly wraps are furs

explanation.surface: Drivers of cars parade expensive coats.
explanation.definitionFit: These are people employed to drive a private motor car for someone else.

clue.text: Fault of Spooner's record company getting support

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words are exchanged

parts.note: Decca is a British record label
a pillow supports the head

explanation.surface: A record label's misdeed is to accept sponsorship.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sin or minor failing is a slight fault.

clue.text: Took notice of the chap meeting two journalists

parts.note: a chap is he
ED is short for editor, a journalist, taken twice

explanation.surface: A man paid attention when he met a pair of reporters.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay attention to advice or a warning is to mind it, the same meaning.

clue.text: 'Charisma' — new yet old term

indicators.note: new tells us the letters of Charisma are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A comment that the word charisma is both a novel and a dated expression.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiquated word or expression no longer in everyday use is an obsolete term.

clue.text: Service with unusually non-U china, say, or cutlery?

definitions.note: the definition gives examples of the thing, two nouns that cannot be counted

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: unusually means not in the usual order, so the letters of non-U are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dinner service of china or cutlery that is not upper-class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-U' is British slang for not upper-class. 'Service' looks like a dinner service but is a church Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: China and cutlery are uncountable nouns taking no plural, grammarians' examples of the type.

clue.text: Pawnbrokers at the forefront of America? Latterly, yes

definitions.text: Pawnbrokers at the forefront of America? Latterly, yes

indicators.note: the pawnbrokers come first, at the front of the other piece

parts.note: uncle is old slang for a pawnbroker

explanation.surface: A quip that pawnbrokers now lead America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker. The whole clue suggests the figure who personifies America has lately become a moneylender.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded, star-spangled cartoon figure personifies the United States and its government.

clue.text: We should leave now for releases

definitions.meaning: a call to depart at once
releases, as a grip is released

explanation.surface: Someone urges leaving, as if granting release.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a call to depart together; the other is the phrasal verb for setting free.

clue.text: Purchase some sheets, it's suggested, for boat

indicators.note: it's suggested hints that the words only resemble the answer when spoken

parts.note: purchase is buy, and a ream is a quantity of paper sheets

explanation.surface: Buying some bed linen or sails for a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient galley with two banks of oars is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Violins getting marks from teacher. Rubbish!

parts.note: fiddles are violins
ticks are the marks a teacher puts on correct work

explanation.surface: Music pupils are graded on their violins, and someone scoffs.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned exclamation of contempt meaning nonsense.

clue.text: Land of Hope? Ruritania

indicators.note: of here means taken out of the words that follow, which hold the letters

explanation.surface: A query whether Ruritania, the fictional kingdom, is the land of hope.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruritania is the imaginary kingdom of Anthony Hope's novel The Prisoner of Zenda, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American country is an example of a land or nation.

clue.text: Visit small river

parts.note: the Tay is a river in Scotland

explanation.surface: A short trip to a little river.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a period spent somewhere as a guest, so a visit.

clue.text: Fruit cores taken from huge saplings

indicators.note: cores are the central parts, so only the middle letters of each word are used

explanation.surface: Fruit with its core removed from big young trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jamaican citrus hybrid of grapefruit and tangerine, so a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Ruling from chap pocketing deliveries to outskirts of Nottingham

indicators.note: pocketing means taking in, so the chap holds the following letters

parts.note: a gent is a chap
in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries

indicators.note: outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters are used

explanation.surface: A judgment made by a man who stashes parcels sent to the edge of Nottingham.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' looks like parcels; it is cricket, where an OVER is six balls bowled.
explanation.definitionFit: Government is the act of ruling a state, so the two nouns share a sense.

clue.text: Mark 5 has to be recalled

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: the clue at 5 down defines spinners, and tops are spinning toys

explanation.surface: A demand that a product numbered 5 be recalled.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' stands for the answer to 5 Down, read as a synonym: spinning tops.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a small stain or blemish, so a mark.

clue.text: Don't learn enough, showing reserve

definitions.meaning: to ... is to study too little
a stand-in actor ready to take over a role

explanation.surface: A student who doesn't revise enough ends up a reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: One reading splits the word as too little study; the other is a theatre stand-in.
